mechanism_narrative: The 12-month change in CPIAUCSL (inflation) is a persistent signal of accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This signal is always active as the 12-month change is computed monthly, and the direction is fixed to positive regardless of inflation rate level.
failure_condition: The positive 20-day forward return rate is below 50% over the entire sample period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% indicates a weak labor market and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the months when UNRATE > 5.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 235) creates a 'stagflation' scenario, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the months when FEDFUNDS < 1.0 AND CPIAUCSL > 235.

mechanism_narrative: During a recession (defined by a quarterly decline in real GDP, GDPC1), the S&P 500 tends to have negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to heightened economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the quarters when GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing output index (INDPRO) above 100 indicates strong industrial production, signaling robust economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the months when INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: The level of housing starts (HOUST) is always positive and serves as a leading indicator of economic activity; a higher level consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The positive 20-day forward return rate is below 50% over the entire sample period.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.0% indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the months when FEDFUNDS > 2.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in private sector employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the months when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises.
